title: Singapore’s toxic haze probe expands to 10 palm oil, forestry firms
text:
Singapore’s toxic haze probe expands to 10 palm oil, forestry firms | South China Morning Post Southeast Asia - Southeast Asia Singapore’s toxic haze probe expands to 10 palm oil, forestry firms 1 Advertisement Singapore Asia Southeast Asia Singapore’s toxic haze probe expands to 10 palm oil, forestry firms 
 Under the Transboundary Haze Act, Singapore can fine locally registered companies up to US$78,000 per day of pollution
 2 -MIN READ 2 -MIN 1 Bloomberg Published: 9:45am, 26 Oct 2026 Singapore has expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies. The National Environment Agency (NEA) sent notices seeking documents and details of land concessions in Indonesia owned by the firms, their firefighting and blaze prevention measures, and their relationship to other relevant companies, according to a Friday statement.
 All 10 Singapore-registered companies were involved in the palm oil or forestry sectors and included Wilmar International, Golden Agri International and First Resources, the agency said.
